records.name: Dorisa
records.facts_used: The Latvian name-rendering manual gives the exact English correspondence Doris → Dorisa. This is a documented spelling relationship between a source-language personal name and its Latvian adaptation; it does not establish every individual bearer’s naming route. The exact row appears in the 2006 manual on printed page 99. This dates the published rendering recommendation. It does not identify the first Latvian birth registration, and earlier dates for other spellings are not transferred to this form.
records.reason: Exact-form evidence supports a reviewed history in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Checked location: PDF 96 / printed 99. Original PDF pages were visually read where used; catalogue transcriptions remain attributed.

records.name: Agatonas
records.facts_used: The dictionary pairs Agatonas with Agathon. Rajandi explains the Greek name through the same “good, kind” meaning as Agatha. This is a link within an older Greek name family, rather than a Lithuanian word-for-word compound. The exact form is documented in the Senn–Salys Lithuanian–German dictionary of 1968, reprinted in Salys’s collected writings in 1983. This is a dated linguistic record of the name and its relationships; it does not identify the first child registered with this spelling.
records.reason: Exact-form evidence supports a reviewed history in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Checked location: Dictionary PDF 211 / printed 196, Agathon; Rajandi PDF 15 / printed 17, Greek agathon good. Original PDF pages were visually read where used; catalogue transcriptions remain attributed.

records.name: Talva
records.facts_used: Rajandi groups Talva with Talvi among newer Estonian nature names, formed in a tradition influenced by Finnish examples. He distinguishes these creations from the separate Taima/Taimi names discussed in the same article. Among adult women changing names in Tallinn in 1935–1940, his account records one choice of Talva. That is a dated example of this exact form. It is not the number of girls born with the name, nor a first-use date borrowed from Taimi.
records.reason: Exact-form evidence supports a reviewed history in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Checked location: PDF 158 / printed 160: nature-name formation, one Tallinn female adult name change 1935–40. Original PDF pages were visually read where used; catalogue transcriptions remain attributed.

records.name: Talvi
records.facts_used: Rajandi includes Talvi among newer Estonian nature names, alongside Talva. He also records the name for both women and men. Sharing an article with Taimi does not make Talvi a derivation of Taimi. His historical account records a woman choosing Talvi in Tallinn in 1935–1940, and also notes later male use in southern Estonia. The contexts remain distinct: a name-change example is not an infant birth count or proof that the spelling has always had only one gender.
records.reason: Exact-form evidence supports a reviewed history in five languages.
